views.claim: Deterministic exposure only; no human decision value measured.

card.claim: Construction candidate: separate seating from restraint. Plywood corner datums and axial stops locate each rod before hand-operated M5 pressure members clamp it against datums; cord tethers movable members/nuts, loops retain them. This replaces tight enclosing clearance, which may restrain yet trap rods before stop contact; performance is unproven.
card.discriminator: If incomplete seating caused the supplied tighter-fit reversal, datum-first should reduce unloaded return error versus enclosing contact. Tightening may improve loaded stability without improving return error. Equal seating with similar return weakens this explanation. The 18 mm substitution may reveal centerline/pointer-offset dependence despite repeatable face seating.
card.probe: Use supplied materials/tools only: six plywood pieces, eight M5 bolts/nuts, four washers, loops and cord. Within 100 fabrication minutes, make one reversible fixture with corner/stop and optional enclosing contact. Verify captive parts, hand-only assembly/adjustment, access, achievable fastening geometry, 90 mm cube envelope; no rod drilling/adhesive/permanent marks. Compare two configurations: five exchanges per original rod, then two 18 mm substitutions each; log duration (under forty seconds required)/unloaded error. Four ten-second 10 N load trials each: initial, fifth exchange of each original rod, final substitution; record escape from 2 mm target. At forty seconds/exchange, only 160 seconds remain for switching/load setup/logging in twenty testing minutes; infeasibility leaves comparison unresolved.
card.uncertainty: Declared fit uncertain: required rod orientation/pointer attachment are unspecified; fixed-face suitability, subdivisions, stiff captive pressure members and fabrication feasibility require verification. Two adverse trials suggest seating without establishing cause. Defeat: inconsistent stop contact, crushing, slip, angular amplification beyond 2 mm, substitution offset, free components or exchanges exceeding forty seconds. Full loaded-return outcome remains unproven.

views.claim: Deterministic exposure only; no human decision value measured.

card.claim: Speculative: clearance-rich seating could restore the pointer more repeatably than visually tight fit, accommodating 18 mm replacement. Replace opposed tight-fit contacts with the same two adjacent plywood datum faces and an insertion stop per rod: end-stop contact, corner seating, hand tightening. Shared plywood cradle, bolt restraint, elastic seating bias and cord-retained hardware would make repeatability depend on seating order, not width.
card.discriminator: Rival: tighter symmetric restraint improves stiffness and return. Datum seating predicts smaller post-exchange displacement despite clearance, including substitution; rival predicts tight-fit superiority. Improved return with increased loaded drift leaves repeatability/restraint dependencies unresolved. Two supplied trials suggest this discriminator, not proof.
card.probe: Using six plywood pieces, eight bolts/nuts, four washers, two loops, 0.5 m cord and permitted tools, fabricate one captive cradle within 100 minutes; cut/drill only plywood. Compare datum-before-tightening versus opposed tightening with identical hardware; counterbalance order. Before timing, verify both pockets/retained hardware fit the 90 mm cube and loosened hardware stays attached. Within 20 testing minutes, each configuration gets twelve exchanges: five per original rod, then two 18 mm substitutions; four 10 N, ten-second load trials. Log stopwatch exchange time, target-card return, loaded displacement and retention. Stop on retention failure; stopped runs establish no performance success.
card.uncertainty: Orientation unspecified: both pockets may not fit. Rigid datums and secure, unobstructive cord retention remain unproved. Hand assembly/adjustment only; no rod drilling, adhesive or permanent marks; preload must avoid permanent indentation. No component may fall free. Defeat: worse return than rival, escape from 2 mm target under load, exchange >=40 seconds, loose components, or exhausted fabrication/testing time. Insufficient measurement resolution/incomplete trials leave outcome unresolved. Enabling experiment, not deployment.
